        *   Classify cylindrical Earth eclipse from inertial spacecraft position and Sun direction.
        *   Normalize Sun direction.
        *   Projection behind Earth is positive when `-r dot sun > 0`. Compute perpendicular miss vector and declare eclipse when behind and miss distance is strictly below Earth radius.
        *   Return projection (`behind_m`), miss distance (`miss_m`), and eclipse flag (`eclipse`).
        *   `NULL -> ADCS_E_NULL; nonfinite/degenerate data or nonpositive radius -> ADCS_E_RANGE.`
        *   Failures set `eclipse=0`, `behind=0`, `miss=INFINITY`.
        *   Normative math: `s = normalize(sun_direction)`, `behind = -position dot s`, `miss_vector = position + behind * s`, `miss = ||miss_vector||`. Eclipse is exactly `(behind > 0) && (miss < earth_radius)`. Radius equality is sunlight.
        *   Prefer GNC primitives.
        *   Context provides types, macros, and helper functions like `adcs_vec3_dot`, `adcs_vec3_norm`, `adcs_vec3_normalize`, `adcs_is_finite_vec3`, etc.
